items.source: run-tests.js reports a Library count that is 30 assets too high
items.title: The suite prints “library: 638 assets (649 catalogued, 11 excluded)”, but the page shows 608. The banner on line 27 filters on `library!==false` alone, while index.html's single visibility line also requires a thumbnail, a fetchable link and, for a Video, media-map playable:true. The tests themselves are fine — they run the engine sliced out of the page, and the suite does load media-map.js — it is only the headline number that measures a different library. That is exactly the count-drift the one-place-decides rule exists to prevent, and it is why 'before → after' numbers in these reports have been quoted from the wrong source. One-line fix: apply the same predicate in the banner, or print both and label them.

items.source: Sakshi's videos and stories — confirm they reach the hub, and whether they feed the trailer
items.title:
Carried from 12 Oct, raised by Aditya and recorded as pending at his request — no action taken. Two things unverified: (1) whether everything she produces actually reaches the Content Hub, or whether stories in particular are published and then lost because nobody downloads them before they expire; (2) whether that material should feed the monthly WhatsApp trailer. TODAY ADDS WEIGHT TO (1): 19 photographs she shot on 8 October only reached Drive on 13 October, five days later, and would have been invisible to every run in between. Nothing is wrong with the pipeline — but the lag means a scan is never a statement about what was shot, only about what has been uploaded.

ANSWERED 14 Oct 2026 for part (1), and the answer is that stories are unrecoverable, not merely untagged. Three stores were checked. ifm-published.json holds 74 posts typed 43 reel / 31 post and ZERO stories, because it is built from the profile grid and the grid never contained them. ig-insights.json does not exist, so the Graph route has never run. And the Graph route would not help retrospectively even once the token is set up: fetch_ig.py reads media_product_type (which does have a STORY value) off the /media edge, but /media does not return stories — those live on a separate /stories edge that lists only what is live in the last 24 hours. There is no archive endpoint. So a story posted yesterday is already gone from every machine-readable source we have or could add.

What that rules out: there is no way to look back and label which of her clips were posted as stories. Of 649 rows exactly one has 'story' in its title, and the Story type is used by 19 rows, all Aakara's. All 18 Stories folders in Drive are Aakara's delivery tree. She has no folder convention, so the catalogue has nothing to read.

What is NOT wrong: her uploads folder is fully accounted for. 'Sakshi uploads' holds 56 files; 40 are catalogued and the other 16 are each named in some row's notes as a deliberate near-dupe skip. Nothing of hers is silently missing. Also correcting an earlier claim made in this session: there is no `source: Sakshi` field. `source` holds Event/In-house/Aakara/Workshop/Certificates, and her attribution is free text in `notes` — 36 rows assert she uploaded the file, 104 more mention her incidentally. Attribution is prose, not queryable.

The only fix is forward-looking and needs a human decision: either she saves each story to her camera roll and drops it in a Stories/ folder the way Aakara already does, or stories stay permanently uncatalogued. Capture at post time is the only moment the data exists.
